channel.description: Writing on intelligence and the institutions that keep culture alive. Published by OSSUS.

item.title: Stories from the Inside
item.description: How a handful of activists trying to get books to one jailed friend became thirty thousand books a year, and why that floor is now cracking.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: Thirty Years & Two Metres Under
item.description: A shy girl hiding fairy books behind the encyclopedias, a man with 23,600 stolen volumes, and the two metre gap where a book can vanish for thirty years.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: Pride & Prejudice
item.description: From a Swedish sorority party to armed anime librarians, the many afterlives of the woman in the mousy cardigan.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: Is There Really A Reading Crisis?
item.description: Sweden still scores above average in reading, and that is exactly what the numbers are hiding.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: AI & Fingerspitzengefühl
item.description: Why the anger I expected at ALA never came, and why we’d refuse to sell Librar to anyone replacing a librarian.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: On Borrowed Time
item.description: On school librarians, the hours that get away from them, and what they would do with just one more.
item.dc:creator: Karin Wannerud

item.title: Notes from a first ALA
item.description: First impressions from four days on the floor of the ALA conference in Chicago.
